req.title: Register rejects duplicate username
req.statement: The system shall render an error message when POST /auth/register is called with a username already present in the users table.

doc.reasoning: The violation was test[4] having kind='negative' but heuristic='BVA'. BVA is a boundary-value technique and must be paired with kind='boundary'. The fix is to change test[4]'s kind from 'negative' to 'boundary', which is semantically correct because that test explicitly probes the boundary between the 200 (error) and 302 (success) status codes — a classic BVA scenario. All other tests are preserved unchanged.

from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

r = client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'anypassword'})

assert b'User test is already registered.' in r.data

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_register_new_unique_username_redirects_to_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    c = app.test_client()
    resp = c.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'brandnewuser', 'password': 'securepass'})
    assert resp.status_code == 302
    assert resp.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'
    assert b'already registered' not in resp.data
    os.unlink(path)

preconditions: Database is initialised with pre-loaded fixture
actions: POST /auth/register with username='newuser' and password='pass1' (first registration)
POST /auth/register with username='newuser' and password='pass2' (duplicate registration)
expected: First POST returns HTTP 302 with Location '/auth/login'
Second POST response body contains exactly 'User newuser is already registered.'
trace: R-FLASKR-006: state transition from unregistered -> registered -> duplicate-rejected

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_register_same_username_twice_in_sequence():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    c = app.test_client()
    r1 = c.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'newuser', 'password': 'pass1'})
    assert r1.status_code == 302
    assert r1.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'
    r2 = c.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'newuser', 'password': 'pass2'})
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    assert b'User newuser is already registered.' in r2.data
    assert b'already registered' in r2.data
    os.unlink(path)

test_register_same_username_twice_in_sequence()

tests.name: test_register_duplicate_does_not_redirect
preconditions: Database is initialised with pre-loaded fixture containing username 'test'
expected: HTTP status code is exactly 200, not 302
Location header is absent or not '/auth/login'
Response body contains the duplicate-user error message
trace: R-FLASKR-006: boundary between success (302) and failure (200) — catches status-code mutations
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_register_duplicate_does_not_redirect():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    c = app.test_client()
    resp = c.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    assert resp.status_code != 302
    assert b'User test is already registered.' in resp.data
    location = resp.headers.get('Location', '')
    assert location != '/auth/login'
    os.unlink(path)

test_register_duplicate_does_not_redirect()
